# Hardware-Adjacent Project Deep Dive

[← NVIDIA](../README.md) · [Every NVIDIA question](../../nvidia.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/hardware-adjacent-project-deep-dive)

`domain-knowledge` `gpu` `infra` `metrics`

---

## Requirements

Be prepared to discuss previous projects at implementation-level depth:

- What the project accomplished and why it was important.
- The technologies, libraries, and infrastructure involved.
- How the system connected with hardware, GPU clusters, or hardware-design processes.
- How GPU usage or compute-resource requirements were quantified.
- Where OpenTelemetry-like instrumentation or monitoring belonged in the system.
- How internally built Python libraries were designed, released, and supported.
- How data flowed through Hive, Iceberg, or comparable table formats.

## Notes

This is more than a standard resume review. Interviewers may devote the entire round to earlier work and request precise technical details.

For HPC or GPU-related work, be ready to discuss cluster-management concepts, CPU-versus-GPU resource accounting, DCGM-like metrics, utilization across workflows, and the importance of those measurements for capacity planning.

For data-platform work, be ready to explain schema changes over time, table organization, partitioning, compaction, backfills, and the rollout of Python modules used by other teams.

## Preparation

- Select two projects and create a one-page technical summary for each covering the goal, architecture, difficult bug, scale, metrics, and trade-offs.
- Draw a diagram for any GPU or HPC cluster project that includes the scheduler, workers, metrics, storage, and users.
- Rehearse follow-up answers involving the API, data schema, deployment route, and operational failure modes.
